BOHEMIA — THE COMMUNITY WALL.

THE BRICK THROUGH THE MIDDLE OF THE GATE IS GONE. You circled it and you were looking at a real bug in the game, not just in my picture. The wall is two cells thick where it runs along the top and bottom of a block, and I was drawing the same gate piece on both of them. Each piece leaves its top edge see-through on purpose, so the wall's stone cap shows above the opening like a lintel. On the lower one that same see-through strip let a course of brick show straight across the gate's waist. It also gave it two doorsteps.

A tall gate is not one piece twice. It is a top and a bottom: cap above, bars running through the join, one doorstep at the floor. Same split the garage bay already uses.

And you said you liked all of them, so all 18 are in the game now, not 11. Every strip below is exactly what the run draws: eight different faces shuffled per cell, pillars on a rhythm, and the gate built the way a real one is.
